Received gifts require growth while remembered witness supports the coming promise

Verses 3–4 say God has given everything needed and great promises. Verses 5–7 list what to add, from faith through to love. Verse 8 gives the result if these qualities are theirs and growing. They will not be idle or unfruitful in knowing the Lord Jesus Christ. Knowledge is meant to bear fruit. Verse 9 says one who lacks them is blind and forgets his cleansing. Verse 10 tells them to make their calling sure.
Promises of freedom conceal greed and renewed slavery when conduct denies the message

Verse 18 says these teachers entice people who are just escaping from error. Verse 19 names the bait: a promise of liberty. It then names the teachers’ real condition: they are bondservants of corruption. The verse gives a general rule to prove it. A person is a slave of whatever overcomes him. Verses 20–22 apply it to those who return to the world’s defilements. Their last state is worse than the first.
The delayed promise calls for patient hope and changed conduct without an exact countdown

Verse 4 gives the mockers’ argument: nothing has changed since the fathers died. Verse 8 answers about time: a thousand years are as a day. Verse 9 answers about motive. The delay is not slowness; it is patience. God does not wish anyone to perish. He wants all to come to repentance. Verse 15 repeats it: count the Lord’s patience as salvation.
